page.overview:
What is Street Fighter?

This article is about the first game in the series. For the series as a whole, see Street Fighter series.

Street Fighter (also more retrospectively known as "Street Fighter I") is an [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcade_video_game arcade] [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fighting_game fighting game] developed by Capcom, released on August 30th, 1987. It is the first competitive fighting game produced by the company and the titular launch title of the Street Fighter series.

Despite being the foundation of the long-running multi-million dollar franchise, the original Street Fighter, while a commercial success in Japan and U.K., was not popular in the U.S. when it was first released, unlike most of its sequels including the phenomenally more successful Street Fighter II: The World Warrior released in 1991. However, the game was innovate for its time and introduced some of the conventions made standard in later titles, such as attack buttons and special command-based techniques. A port for the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TurboGrafx-16#TurboGrafx-CD/CD-ROM%C2%B2 TurboGrafx-CD] was released under the title Fighting Street in 1988. It has also been re-released multiple times by Capcom in emulated arcade classic compilations.

Although not forgotten among the Street Fighter fandom today, as it predates Street Fighter II's establishment for proper controls in the fighting game genre and its gameplay is rather basic in comparison to later installments of the series, the original game is notorious for being difficult to perform special moves as well as major balance issues of fighters defeating opponents very quickly when landing in rapid succession, leading some to believe it doesn't age well.
